rv.q: The show is, paradoxically, a daring Coward.
Tracy-Ann Oberman and James Dreyfus excel in a gender-flipped, transatlantic take on Coward
What elevates it is Oberman’s wonderfully detailed performance and a conceptual rethink that allows the play to feel closer to its authentic queer self.
Oberman's bold reimagining feels fresh and distinctive while retaining all the wit, glamour and deliciously theatrical spirit of the original.
There is much to admire in Oberman’s bold reimagining of the classic play and her performance as Geri, but the situation never quite rings true...

cn.t: Critics praise this gender-switched, 1970s New York reimagining of Coward's comedy, with Tracy-Ann Oberman delivering a hilariously brilliant performance as Geri Essendine in Lindsay Posner's smart, dazzling production.
